_arch_note: exp_n_0121 (nap8/tph128, 1.1914552 at 67,351,692 params over 16k) with ONE architectural change: the FFN-slot LUT module is HyperplaneMHL instead of CompressionMHL's FastMHL. HyperplaneMultiHeadLUT generalizes FastMultiHeadLut -- each table selects its row via nap LEARNED affine sign tests 1[<w_i,x>+b_i>0] instead of fixed anchor-pair differences x[a]-x[b] -- so the swap is inside CompressionMHL's compress/per-head-LUT/decompress sandwich, not a replacement of the sandwich. See local_hyperplane_compression.py; shared src/spiky/lutorch/ is untouched. Every other hyperparameter is held identical to exp_n_0121: H4, inner_in 48, inner_out 48, nap 8 (256 cells), tph 128, untied head, forward_mode hard, learnable_temps, init noise 1e-3, base seed 1000, depth 6, n_embd 384, n_head 6, seq 512, vocab 32768, lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, seed 1, device_batch 12 / grad_accum 4 (effective batch 24,576). hyperplane_init=anchor_pairs makes each hyperplane reproduce its anchor pair EXACTLY at step 0 (w_i = e_a - e_b, b_i = 0, no noise), so the model starts bit-for-bit as the FastMHL exp_n_0121 started from and diverges only as the hyperplanes learn -- which is what makes the step-for-step A/B meaningful. Anchors: exp_n_0121 (direct parent, step-aligned over the first 4k), exp_n_0119 1.18386, exp_n_0084 dense-V 1.19866.
_run_length_note: SHORT SCREEN: 4,000 steps instead of exp_n_0121's 16,000. The LR schedule is deliberately NOT recomputed for 4,000 -- lr_schedule_steps stays 16000, so warmup is 1,600 and the cosine runs over 16,000 exactly as in exp_n_0121. Recomputing it (warmup 400, cosine finishing at 4,000) would change the learning rate at EVERY step, and the entire readout of this run is the step-for-step delta against exp_n_0121's curve; each aligned point would then confound the module swap with a different optimizer trajectory. With the schedule held, step k here and step k there differ only in the LUT module. Consequence, stated plainly: this run stops mid-anneal (LR ~0.86 of peak at step 4,000), so its final number is a trajectory probe, not a converged result, and it is NOT comparable to exp_n_0121's 1.1914552 final. Both runs eval every 200 steps, so the first 20 evals align exactly with no interpolation.
_mem_note: device_batch_size 12 / grad_accum 4 inherited unchanged from exp_n_0121 (effective batch 24,576 tokens identical). HyperplaneMHL's soft backward must additionally produce gradients for hyperplane_weight [n_tables, nap, inner_in] and hyperplane_bias, on top of the [N, n_tables, 2^nap] surrogate FastMHL already needed, so it is strictly heavier than exp_n_0121 at the same batch. Verified before launch by a smoke that mirrors a REAL training step -- the full grad_accum=4 micro-batch loop on real data, plus a real evaluate_bpb -- rather than single micro-batches, which is the trap that let exp_g_0028 pass a smoke and then OOM before step 1.
